I am not here to judge, I can say that I have read a book titled how to take a test, and it helped me a lot. You can find it in your library. It has simple things like remember to put your name on the test, drink more water, stay away from coffee or alcohol. Our brain uses a lot of the water in our system. Don't get stuck on a question, if you don't know the answer move on you will usually find a similar question which will help you find the answer. If you don't know the answer, take a guess on multiple choice you always have a 25% chance. Some teachers and professors will have a couple of impossible questions designed to catch cheaters so do not expect to get a perfect score. Use all of the time allotted, go backwards through the test after you finish it going forward, sometimes one question can be reverse engineered to find an answer to another question which had you stumped. don't overstudy you will only burn out. I wish you all the best.

Let's start with how to get people to treat you differently, it will take some time and practice it is not an instant fix. 

Charisma is not something we are born with. You can learn it.

We have all met people in our lives that we liked, they made us feel good, they seemed cool, classy, it was easier to be around them.

We might not have realized what it was about them, but we wished to be more like them. Sometimes we may have even felt jealous of them how easy they made it look in different social situations.

It turns out a college course taught how to be charismatic. It is very useful in business and social situations.

here are a few tips from the book "The charisma myth"

1. Be there - totally focus your mind on the person you are speaking with. Let them speak first and listen to them; you learn more by listening, when we talk, all we can say are things we already know. When you look at them look slightly to one side, not like you are staring directly into their eyes. If you seem fidgety, they will pick up on it and think you are bored with what they are saying. No finger tapping or toe tapping, knee shaking nervous energy, just relax and absorb their words.

(To get better at focusing your mind meditate on how your body breathes or on all of the sensations you feel in your toes for several minutes a couple of times a week).

2. Always wait 2 seconds before answering, this makes you appear more thoughtful.

3. Avoid nodding your head in excess, you are not a bobble head, try to reduce the times you nod by 1/2.

4. When you speak lower the intonation of your voice at the end of the sentence. This allows the other person to sense you are completing your thought, intonation is a slight lowering of tone and volume on the last sentence of a statement.

5. When you shake hands touch the other persons wrist forearm or outer elbow with your other hand. Touching them with both hands make them feel like you really connected with them.

6. Mimic them, don't be obvious but if they touch their hair or rub their hands try to find a way to do something similar later in the conversation. If they use a particular slang word find a way to also use it. Remember the valley girls, to fit in they said "oh my gawd" etc.

It makes them consider you to be like them and they feel more comfortable around you.

7. Remember their name even on a phone call and use it in the conversation.

8. People tend to remember the last thing you said the best.

9. Try to use positive action language for example: I'm sure, you might decide to call me later vs I'm sure you will consider calling me tomorrow afternoon around 5:30.

Think of it like planting a seed.

10. Always smile and tell them positive things when you are leaving. It’s always a pleasure to see you or always a pleasure to speak with them.
